scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they cannot reach pc2
(200.1.1.2) or anything outside their own subnet since "cleaning
up" their network settings -- their pings now fail with
"Destination Host Unreachable". Oddly, pc1 pings its gateway
195.11.14.1 fine. The partner side reports pc2's pings to pc1
time out, while everything else there works. What's wrong?

injection.action: point pc1's default route at a nonexistent gateway (.254)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc1 default route / gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc1's default route points at 195.11.14.254, an address
  that exists on no device (the real gateway is router1's eth1 at
  195.11.14.1). ARP for .254 gets no answer, so every off-subnet
  packet from pc1 dies locally with "Destination Host Unreachable".
  On-subnet traffic (the connected 195.11.14.0/24 route) still
  works, which is why pc1 can ping 195.11.14.1. The network side
  is fully healthy: router1 still advertises 195.11.14.0/24, the
  eBGP session is Established, and pc2's pings ARE delivered to
  pc1 -- but pc1's replies chase the phantom gateway and are never
  sent, so pc2 sees timeouts.
Localization: pc1
Root cause: pc1's default route points at nonexistent gateway
  195.11.14.254 instead of 195.11.14.1
Fix: `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev eth0` on pc1
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore pc1's default route -- `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev
eth0` on pc1. Off-subnet connectivity returns immediately; no router or BGP
change is needed.

bonus-exonerates-network: verifies the routers, the eBGP session and the advertised prefixes are healthy -- the fault is confined to pc1's own routing table

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is pc1’s host routing configuration. On pc1, the default gateway is misconfigured to 195.11.14.254 (ip route shows “default via 195.11.14.254 dev eth0”), while its local router is 195.11.14.1 (router1 eth1 = 195.11.14.1/24). This wrong next-hop is not present on the subnet, so when pc1 tries to reach any off-subnet destination (e.g., 200.1.1.2 or “outside”), it ARPs for 195.11.14.254, gets no reply, and the kernel returns “Destination Host Unreachable.” That matches the user’s symptom.

Mechanism for the partner’s observation: pc2’s pings to 195.11.14.2 are forwarded correctly across the routers (both routers have BGP-learned routes: router1 has 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2; router2 has 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1). The echo request reaches pc1, but pc1’s echo reply must go off-subnet; it follows the bad default route to 195.11.14.254, fails ARP, and never leaves, so pc2 sees timeouts. Local reachability (pc1 to 195.11.14.1) still works because it is on-link and does not use the default route.

Root cause: pc1’s default route was set to a nonexistent gateway (195.11.14.254) during the “cleanup.”

Corrective fix: On pc1, replace the default route with the real gateway:
- ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev eth0
Also remove any stale entry to 195.11.14.254 and, if needed, update persistent network config to use 195.11.14.1 as the default gateway. After this change, pc1↔pc2 connectivity will be restored.
